text:
lina: Heads-up — AtlasLogistics (acct atlas-prod) opened a ticket: their nightly embedding job started failing intermittently after they bumped to redwood-python v1.9.0. Error in their pipeline: 'SchemaMismatch: index expected 1024 but got 1536' on about 12% of batches. They don't set model explicitly. Posting the sanitized snippet they attached.

customer-rep: Sanitzed snippet from Atlas (they run Faiss ingest):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="***")
lines = load_lines('to_index.txt')  # ~50k lines
resp = client.embeddings.create(input=lines, batch_size=200, timeout=120)
# later during indexing: SchemaMismatch: expected 1024 got 1536
```

sam: I pulled API traces — atlas-prod (last 6h): 320 /v1/embeddings calls. 210 omitted model param, 110 explicitly set model="embed-medium-v1". Backend responses include dims 1024 (278), 1536 (28), 512 (14). The 1536 and 512 responses line up with the failing batches. Also noticed a spike in requests routed to embed-xlarge-v3 during high concurrency windows, which explains the 1536.

support-bot: log note: routing policy recently had a short-lived capacity rebalancing across tiles; fallback to smaller/alternate variants observed. Creating internal trace id 0x7f3c for the failing request group.

ben: Repro attempt (quick):
- py v1.9.0, calling client.embeddings.create with a single huge array (200 items) and default model -> occasionally get mixed-length vectors in the same response array.
- If I force chunking to 32 items per call, behavior stable.

lina: Customer also reported an unexpected billing increase — some calls routed to embed-xlarge-v3 (higher per-token/per-embed cost). They noticed invoices inflated the night of the incident.

eng-lead: Important: two separate issues here that exacerbate each other: (1) runtime routing can split a large logical request across replicas that run different model variants (and those variants have different embedding dims), (2) SDKs/clients that do aggressive retries or merge responses can end up mixing dims or double-billing if a fallback succeeds with a costlier model.

sam: Quick debug detail: HTTP keep-alive + connection reuse sometimes resulted in sub-chunks being proxied to different backend processes. When those processes are running different model binaries (or quantized variants), the output dims differ.

ben: I also reproduced a subtle Node bug: in redwood-js 2.4.0, when running under certain stream buffer conditions we switch to a streaming upload path which the router scores differently, and that triggers the large-variant route. Patch idea: avoid switching upload path for JSON arrays, normalize headers.

lina: Customer wants immediate help — their ingest job writes into an immutable schema so even one mixed-dim batch fails the whole nightly job. I gave them a short mitigation: pin the model parameter to embed-medium-v1 and re-run with batch_size=32.

customer-rep: Atlas confirmed they pinned model and reduced batch size; errors stopped. They want a written explanation and an ETA for a fix so they can unpin later if we guarantee consistent dims.

eng-lead: Action items:
- runtime: ensure a single logical request (one client call) is never split across model variants with differing embedding dims; if no single compatible variant available, fail the request with clear error.
- runtime: add response header X-Redwood-ModelId and X-Redwood-Embedding-Dim to every embeddings response for immediate observability.
- sdk: JS/Python/Go point patches to (a) warn when model omitted under high-throughput calls, (b) avoid serialization paths that influence routing, (c) recommend chunking helpers in docs.
- billing: add a note in billing logs if a request unexpectedly upsells to a higher-cost model due to fallback so customers can audit.

ben: Temporary SDK snippets I shared with Atlas (sanitized) — safe patterns for now: chunk, assert dims, controlled retries.

Python (chunk + assert + retry):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import time
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="***")
EXPECTED = 1024
chunks = [lines[i:i+32] for i in range(0, len(lines), 32)]
embeds = []
for c in chunks:
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            r = client.embeddings.create(input=c, model="embed-medium-v1", timeout=90)
            for item in r.data:
                if len(item['embedding']) != EXPECTED:
                    raise ValueError(f"unexpected dim {len(item['embedding'])}")
            embeds.extend([d['embedding'] for d in r.data])
            break
        except Exception as e:
            if attempt == 3:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.2 * (attempt+1))
```

JS (avoid streaming path + pin model):

```ts
import Redwood from 'redwood'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW })
async function safeEmbeds(texts:string[]){
  const out:number[][] = []
  for(let i=0;i<texts.length;i+=32){
    const chunk = texts.slice(i,i+32)
    const resp = await client.embeddings.create({ input: chunk, model: 'embed-medium-v1', timeout: 60000 })
    resp.data.forEach(d=>{ if(d.embedding.length !== 1024) throw new Error('dim mismatch') })
    out.push(...resp.data.map(x=>x.embedding))
  }
  return out
}
```

Go (chunk + validate dims + exponential backoff):

```go
for _, chunk := range chunks {
  var resp *redwood.EmbeddingsResponse
  var err error
  for attempt := 0; attempt < 5; attempt++ {
    resp, err = client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, redwood.EmbeddingsParams{Model: "embed-medium-v1", Input: chunk})
    if err == nil { break }
    time.Sleep(time.Duration(100*(1<<attempt)) * time.Millisecond)
  }
  if err != nil { return err }
  for _, d := range resp.Data {
    if len(d.Embedding) != 1024 { return fmt.Errorf("unexpected dim %d", len(d.Embedding)) }
  }
}
```

lina: I told Atlas to add a dim assertion in their job to fail fast and avoid corrupting the nightly index. Also recommended they add a billing alert for spikes.

sam: Filed ENG ticket RW-ENG-emb-3330 with the runtime team to enforce consistent-dim behavior for single logical requests and to add the diagnostic headers. Assigned to eng-runtime team; requested hotfix ETA.

dev-bot: RW-ENG-emb-3330 created and linked to support case SUP-96650.

eng-lead: Tentative plan: runtime hotfix to avoid heterogeneous-dim splits this week; SDK warnings patch in next 48 hours; billing audit note in next release.

customer-rep: Atlas is happy with the workaround and asks to be notified when the hotfix and SDK patches are live.

lina: I'll follow-up in this thread when PRs land and once billing has posted a clarifying note. Closing interim loop. :thumbsup: reactions from sam, ben, eng-lead
